newsitem.title: UK: Jourdan urges rejection of Abell plans.
newsitem.headline: Jourdan urges rejection of Abell plans.

text.p: UK consumer products group Thomas Jourdan Plc said on Friday that it was urging shareholders to vote against plans by David Abell to replace the chairman Keith Whitten and non-executive directors with Abell and his associate Jonathon Pither.
Abell, formerly chairman and chief executive of Suter Plc, and Kemira Coatings Investments Ltd own 28 percent of Thomas Jourdan.
Thomas Jourdan said that the resolutions put forward by Abell will be voted on at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on May 20.

"Your board is very concerned that Mr Abell and his supporters have been able to acquire over 30 percent of Thomas Jourdan in such a way that they have so far avoided any obligation to make a bid," said chairman Keith Whitten in a statement to shareholders.
"If Mr Abell were to succeed, he would gain control of Thomas Jourdan without having made an offer to shareholders," said Whitten.
